subject.title: improve(ui): restructure Settings around user-facing pages with full agent parity

question: Should OpenClaw permanently permit the system agent, behind exact-operation approval, to write the newly allowed config paths and uninstall plugins that are not on the active inference route?
rationale: This PR intentionally changes the durable authorization boundary rather than only correcting an implementation defect; source-level review cannot determine the repository’s desired operator policy or acceptable compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Sponsor the expanded approval boundary
options.body: Approve the documented operator-parity policy after the two functional defects are fixed and the upgrade/security behavior is demonstrated.

options.title: Keep the narrower policy
options.body: Retain the existing denylist and typed setup flows for plugin and routing-related changes, limiting this PR to the settings-information architecture.

options.title: Split policy from UI redesign
options.body: Land a narrower settings-navigation PR and route the persistent preference and system-agent authorization changes through a dedicated design review.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the expanded approval boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the documented operator-parity policy after the two functional defects are fixed and the upgrade/security behavior is demonstrated.

likelyOwner.reason: The assignee authored the proposed settings and system-agent policy changes and is the best available routing candidate from the supplied history.
